column3: Covers how users and bots manage “who has the floor.” Includes intentional interruptions, accidental interruptions, backchannels, overlap, latency-driven repetition, and cases where the bot speaks too early or waits too long.
Covers moments where the user pauses but has not finished speaking. Includes filled pauses, silent thinking, lookup pauses, memory search, breath pauses, and chunked reading of numbers or IDs.
Covers natural imperfections in spontaneous speech. Includes false starts, restarts, repetitions, stutters, abandoned phrases, and cases where the user corrects or replaces a value mid-sentence.

column2: Non-Speech Sounds That Look Like Speech Events
column3: Covers acoustic events that are not meaningful speech but may trigger the bot’s speech detection. Includes coughs, sighs, laughter, mouth sounds, keyboard noise, door slams, traffic, dogs, babies, or household noise.

Covers speech that may be human but not necessarily directed at the bot. Includes side conversations, third-party helpers, speakerphone calls, TV or radio speech, children interrupting, and call-center floor noise.

Covers telephony and device-specific issues that distort the call. Includes speakerphone echo, low-bandwidth audio, packet loss, mute/unmute, Bluetooth switching, hold music, DTMF keypad input, voicemail, and bot-to-IVR interactions.

Covers high-risk information capture. Includes names, dates, times, emails, addresses, account numbers, payment amounts, spelled values, digit corrections, and ambiguous numbers like “fifteen” vs “fifty.”

Covers cases where the user’s intent changes, is unclear, or needs repair. Includes multi-intent turns, indirect answers, contradictory answers, “never mind,” clarification requests, user corrections, and requests for a human agent.

Covers emotional and social signals that affect the conversation. Includes frustration, anger, anxiety, sarcasm, distrust, privacy concerns, embarrassment, laughter, distress, or the user questioning whether the bot is legitimate.

Covers differences in how people speak. Includes accents, dialects, code-switching, fast speech, slow speech, soft speech, shouting, stuttering, dysarthric speech, older adult speech patterns, children’s voices, and other accessibility-related variation.

Covers user behaviors that are triggered by poor bot design. Includes barge-ins caused by long prompts, repetition caused by latency, frustration caused by ignored corrections, and unnatural responses caused by rigid menu-style questions.

Covers high-risk moments involving user permission, privacy, security, and escalation. Includes interrupted disclosures, partial consent, refusal to provide sensitive information, over-sharing sensitive data, authentication fatigue, and requests for a human during sensitive flows.
